### Problem

A fix to the engine reaches no repository, this one included, until a person accepts a release issue and a person tags it and moves `v7`. Seven minors went out in five days (v7.1.0 to v7.7.0), each with its own issue, pull request and tag by hand; on 2026-11-01 the autopilot's own unsticking fixes (#551) waited on #554 and #555 and on the tag. This repository also runs two versions of its engine: `pull-request.yml` calls `./` (main) while `issues.yml` and `issue-triage.yml` call `@v7`, so a fix works for one trigger and not for the other until the tag moves. And nothing tries a release before every repository runs it: on 2026-11-01 v7.9.0 asked the callers for a permission they do not grant, every repository's `Issues` workflow failed at startup, and a person noticed it and moved `v7` back by hand (#585). The same day, #589 changed this repository's `issues.yml` and the engine together, and every `Issues` run here failed at startup until v7.10.0, because the caller is read from main and the engine from `@v7`; and four large pull requests on the same core files (#567, #569, #584, #589) kept putting one another in conflict. `docs/versioning.md` says `v7` moves "once a change ran end to end in the sandbox", but that is a step a person does by hand, on a repository (sandbox-wordpress-plugin) that is a product's sandbox, with nothing defined about what must pass.

### Scope

- A test repository, declared in `org.yml` as `test-repo`, by default `<org>-test` (`diluxone-test` here), so another organisation gets its own without changing the engine. It is of a kind of its own, `engine-test` (`kinds/engine-test/`), whose pack holds as data what sets it apart: an identity that may accept issues there and nowhere else, the autopilot in a fixed-change mode that calls no model, its issues and pull requests cleaned up after each run, and nothing ever published from it. The daily drift check fails if a repository of that kind is also a product, or if the test identity can accept in any other repository.
- The release scenarios, as data in this repository: one per pair of a reusable workflow and an event a shipped caller wires, and one per transition of the autopilot's state machine (#561), each with the issue or pull request it opens and what must happen. They cover at least: an issue opened complete and incomplete; accepted, sealed and the autopilot starting; the PRD edited after it was accepted; a decision's sub-issues starting without acceptance; `/claim` and a claim released; a bug reproduced and fixed, and one not reproduced; the autopilot's pull request (`Closes`, branch, title); a question answered by a comment and the autopilot going on with no label; a stop, a hint and `autopilot:continue`; a pull request in conflict; review changes asked and made; a pull request from a fork running without secrets; the required checks; the merge queue; a low-risk change merging on its own and a high-risk one waiting for a person; a release issue opening its pull request; the drift check; adopting a repository. A check run by the scripts job fails when a pair or a transition has no scenario. A bug that reached the repositories after a release (#585) adds its scenario in its fix.
- A static check before any run: every job of a reusable workflow asks for no more permissions, and no input or secret beyond what the callers `sync-repos.py callers` writes and the workflow templates give it (#585 starts it with permissions).
- The release lane: once main is green, it points a lightweight `v7-next` tag at the candidate, the test repository (which calls `@v7-next`) runs every scenario, and only when all pass does the lane open the release pull request, merge it, tag `vX.Y.Z` and move `v7` (lightweight, never annotated). A breaking change (a `!`) runs the scenarios too and then waits on a person.
- After `v7` moves, for 30 minutes the lane watches every adopted repository for runs that end in `startup_failure` or fail on the engine's own steps; on the first one it moves `v7` back to the previous release, opens a bug with the failed run's link, and says so on the release.
- The installer (`docs/installing.md` and what it runs) creates the test repository, adopts it (#562), enables the test identity there, and runs every scenario once, so an organisation sees that its installation works before its first real issue.
- This repository's own callers use one ref.
- One change to the engine's core at a time: the core's files are a list in the organisation's configuration (#568); when an open autopilot pull request already touches one of them, the autopilot does not start another issue whose Spec touches the core, and says on it that it waits for that pull request, starting it once that pull request merges or closes.

### Out of scope

- Whether the code the autopilot writes is good: the scenarios try the flow, not the model; each real pull request's review keeps that.
- The products' releases and their publishing, which stay as they are.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given `org.yml` without `test-repo`, when the engine reads it, then the test repository is `<org>-test`; given `test-repo: acme-sandbox`, then it is `acme-sandbox`.
- C2: Given a reusable workflow and event pair wired by a shipped caller, or a transition of the state machine, with no scenario, when the scripts job runs, then it fails and names the pair or the transition.
- C3: Given a reusable workflow whose job asks for a permission, input or secret its shipped caller does not give, when the scripts job runs, then it fails and names the workflow, the job and what is missing.
- C4: Given a fix merged into main with main green, when the release lane runs and every scenario passes in the test repository at `v7-next`, then `vX.Y.Z` is tagged, `v7` points at it (lightweight) and its GitHub Release is published, with no person's step.
- C5: Given a candidate for which one scenario fails, when the release lane runs, then `v7` does not move, nothing is tagged, and a bug is opened naming the scenario and its run.
- C6: Given `v7` just moved and an adopted repository whose run ends in `startup_failure` within 30 minutes, when the watch sees it, then `v7` points at the previous release again and a bug is opened with the run's link.
- C7: Given a merged change marked breaking whose scenarios pass, when the release lane runs, then it opens the release issue for a person and tags nothing.
- C8: Given a repository of kind `engine-test` that is also listed as a product, or the test identity able to accept in another repository, when the drift check runs, then it fails and names it.
- C9: Given a new organisation following `docs/installing.md`, when the installer finishes, then its test repository exists, is adopted, and every scenario ran there once with its result shown.
- C10: Given this repository's workflows, when their `uses:` are read, then every call of its own engine uses the same ref.
- C11: Given an open autopilot pull request that touches a core file, when another issue whose Spec touches the core reaches the autopilot, then it waits with a comment naming that pull request, and starts once it merges or closes.

### Criticality

Normal
